text: At the Thessaly Weir yesterday morning, maintenance crews confirmed to the Gazette that the gate structure diverts the Callan River into the south irrigation channel. Standing beside the control box at 8:15 a.m., foreman Lila Mendt said the system had been running at full draw since Tuesday to keep downstream plots watered during the dry spell. The weir’s steel sluice was opened to 42 percent, according to the board posted on site, sending a steady brown-green flow into the canal. Nearby farmer Jonas Pell told me he could hear the current before sunrise and said the diversion usually means “a better week for the east fields.” No other river feeds the structure.
